title: [Ops][Feature][MRV2] Add early kernel and NZ warmup for Model Runner V2
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR enables early kernel warmup and NZ format-cast warmup for Model Runner V2 (MRv2).
Specifically:
- It integrates `start_early_kernel_warmup`, `join_early_kernel_warmup`, `start_nz_warm_thread`, and `join_nz_warm_thread` into `NPUModelRunner.load_model` in `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py` to overlap Triton compilation and NZ format-cast lazy initialization with weight loading.
- It updates `early_kernel_warmup.py` to skip v1-only rejection sampler and penalty kernels when `use_v2_model_runner` is enabled, only warming up the shared `rms` kernel.
- It adds unit tests to verify that only the required kernels are warmed up for MRv2 and that warmup threads are properly joined even if weight loading fails.
- It updates the documentation to clarify that rejection sampler and penalty kernels are skipped by the v2 model runner.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added unit tests in `tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_early_kernel_warmup.py` to verify that only the `rms` kernel is warmed up when `use_v2_model_runner` is True.
- Added unit tests in `tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2.py` to verify that warmups are started and joined correctly during `load_model`, including the failure path.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change involves
  boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max values,
  off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable, I
  added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or `tests/e2e/`.
- [x] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths (exceptions,
  timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [x] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.
